text: 🇲🇽🚆 "Break-even means they don't require any additional budget support." "...the revenues allow them to operate and maintain their services, and they are all in line with the planning done from the very first moment." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 8, 2026 The state companies run by the Defense Ministry reported: Tren Maya has carried 2.94 million passengers since December 2023, and its revenue grew 96% in 2025 to 541 million pesos. "...and with salaries equivalent to what a doctor earns in our country, and they are in places where they are needed, more remote places, where they help us care for the population." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 8, 2026 Asked about staffing Mexico's plan for 12,000 neighborhood clinics, Sheinbaum said the call for 20,000–23,000 health professionals already has 78,000 applicants, mainly Mexican doctors. And the trains are doing well, the highways are doing well, the water projects are doing well." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 8, 2026 INEGI's latest survey: the share of adults who feel unsafe in their own neighborhood or locality fell from 50.6% in 2018 to 35.9% in 2026, down 11.4% in the last year alone. Perceived insecurity in their municipality dropped from 70.3% in 2019 to 60.9%.

🇲🇽📊 <u>INFLATION 3.45% IN SEPTEMBER, BELOW FORECASTS; CORE AT LOWEST SINCE MARCH 2025</u>

INEGI reports annual inflation of 3.45% for September, up from 3.26% in August but less than analysts expected. Tomatoes (+30.25% in the month), onions (+23%) and LP gas drove the rise. Core inflation, the measure Banxico watches, fell from 3.88% to 3.75%, its lowest level since March 2025. Headline inflation stays inside Banxico's 2–4% band, and El Financiero reports open debate inside the central bank over whether to keep cutting rates.

🇲🇽✊ <u>CDMX REPLACES SHELTERS WITH "CARE COMMUNITIES" FOR 2,000 HOMELESS PEOPLE</u>

Clara Brugada's government presented "Una Nueva Mirada": four Comunidades de Cuidados with room for more than 2,000 people living on the street. The first opens in January 2027. Instead of crowded dormitories there will be small rooms, spaces where families can stay together, women-only areas, mental health and addiction care, free medicines, job training and a route to housing. Some will even let residents keep their pets.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>MILK AND MEDICINE FOR CUBA: NEW DRIVE AT THE MONUMENTO A LA REVOLUCIÓN</u>

While Washington seizes fuel shipments bound for the island, Mexicans are lining up again at the Monumento a la Revolución in Mexico City. The Colectivo Solidaridad Militante Va por Cuba opened its sixth collection drive for milk and medicines today. It runs through October 11, timed to the 59th anniversary of Che Guevara's death. Tons of aid donated by Mexican citizens have already been shipped to Cuba in recent months.
